title: Recover from unknown documentation URLs through the real site search

index.observed: 64 pages indexed covering all 63 expected destinations; 404.html carries no data-pagefind-body so the indexer excludes it by contract (count unchanged from the pre-recovery candidate).

red.observed: 15/15 cases fail on the pre-implementation candidate: the served title never equals the manuscript title, apps/docs/dist/404.html is absent, and the recovery search control never resolves. No infrastructure failures.

green.observed: All 15 cases pass across chromium-desktop, chromium-mobile and chromium-nojs with retries 0: fresh run-specific unknown /docs/ URLs serve the custom 404 with the real manuscript title, explanation and hint; the emitted dist/404.html byte-matches the manuscript and the system file stays outside the docs collection and ordinary docs navigation; Search the site opens the shared aria-modal dialog <=300ms on the island's own activation clock (independent of index readiness) with the search input focused; the real Pagefind index settles 'message' and keyboard selection reaches /components/message/ at HTTP 200 with its own h1 and substantive content; Escape restores focus to the Search the site control; ordinary-page and recovery-page searches load the same production /pagefind/ module and both return Message; completed manuscript-derived queries exclude /404, /404.html and every run-specific unknown URL; dark and light themes selected through the real ThemeToggle persist onto fresh unknown URLs with the shared header, footer and recovery links; and the no-JavaScript project reads the manuscript and reaches /components and /registry at HTTP 200 through the plain links with zero Pagefind requests and the JS-only control hidden.

acceptance.AC-1: proven: fresh run-specific unknown /docs/ URLs serve the manuscript through the custom 404; Search the site opens the shared aria-modal dialog with the 300ms island-clock budget measured independently of Pagefind readiness (the island clocks showModal alone and starts the index in parallel), with the search input focused; the real index settles 'message', keyboard selection reaches /components/message/ at HTTP 200 with its own h1 and substantive content; chromium-nojs proves the readable recovery surface with zero Pagefind requests.
acceptance.AC-2: proven: dist/404.html emitted and byte-compared against the real system manuscript (title, explanation, hint); the manuscript stays outside the docs collection and ordinary docs navigation; dark and light selections made through the real ThemeToggle control persist onto fresh unknown URLs with the shared header, footer and recovery links.
acceptance.AC-3: proven: Escape closes recovery search and restores focus to the Search the site control (in-page activeElement observation); ordinary-page and recovery-page searches both load the production /pagefind/ module and both return Message at /components/message/; completed manuscript-derived queries (missing-page title + distinctive hint phrase) return URL lists that exclude /404, /404.html and every current-run unknown /docs/ URL, recorded with real result counts after settled index completion.
acceptance.AC-4: proven: the manuscript explanation and shared shell remain readable with JavaScript disabled and zero Pagefind resources; the plain Components link reaches /components at HTTP 200 with rendered family content and the plain Registry link reaches /registry at HTTP 200 with the real ledger; the JS-only search control stays hidden without JavaScript.

known_blockers.blocker: Run-order hazard (inherited from ORI-AST-004): any astro build wipes dist/pagefind; the task-owned indexer ran after the last build before every preview-backed lane. CI owns this ordering.
